welcome.name: Engr. Robert M. Fabella
message: Welcome to the official website of the Municipality of Calatrava. This portal is part of our commitment to open, accessible, and accountable governance.
Here you can transact with our offices, follow the programs and projects of your local government, and reach us directly. Our doors — and our records — are open to you.

vision: A premiere gateway of the province with vibrant, productive and sustainable eco-tourism, whose people are God-loving and living in a safe, peaceful, healthy and ecologically-balanced environment guided by dynamic, transparent and responsive leaders.
mission: The local government of Calatrava shall: ensure and support the preservation and enrichment of the Filipino culture; enhance public moral among the people; promote health and safety in the community; ensure the right of the people to a balanced ecology; encourage and support the development of appropriate and new scientific and technological capabilities; promote economic prosperity and social justice; create a self-reliant community; and preserve the comfort and convenience of the inhabitants.
_missionNote: The Citizen's Charter states the mission as eight numbered commitments. `mission` keeps them as one sentence for anywhere that needs a single string; `missionLead` + `missionPoints` are the same text split back out, which is what the homepage renders — a list is far easier to scan than a long centred paragraph.

mandate: To keep with the policy of the State, Republic Act No. 11032, known as the "Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018," has been adopted by the Local Government Unit to establish its own Citizen's Charter containing the procedures, fees, processing time, and requirements for our services.
servicePledge: We, the officials and employees of the Municipality of Calatrava, Romblon, pledge and commit to deliver the quality public services as promised in this Citizen's Charter. Specifically, we will serve with integrity; be prompt and timely; display procedures, fees and charges; provide adequate and correct information; be consistent in applying the rules; provide a feedback mechanism; be polite and courteous; demonstrate sensitivity, appropriate behaviour and professionalism; wear proper uniform and identification; be available during office hours; respond to complaints; provide a comfortable waiting area; and treat everyone equally.
history: Long before it carried its present name, the settlement on the northern coastal plain of Tablas Island was known as Andagao, after a medicinal plant that grew in abundance along its shores. The name survives today in the LGU's own email address and in local usage.

Around 1810, the first settlers reached Andagao — Simaranhons, Sibalenhons and Bantoanons crossing from Banton, Simara and Romblon island in search of land better suited to farming, later joined by Asi-speaking migrants from Odiongan. By about 1838 the settlement had been organised as a community attached to Odiongan, and in 1839 Padre Jose Aznar oversaw the building of its first Roman Catholic church.

Andagao was first proclaimed a municipality in 1853, when the District of Romblon was created. The status did not hold: in 1868 it was reduced to a visita and annexed to Badajoz — the town known today as San Agustin. On 14 June 1881, during the term of the Spanish military governor Don Jose Fernandez de Terran, Andagao was renamed Calatrava after the medieval Military Order of Calatrava.

A second proclamation came on 4 June 1943 under the wartime revolutionary government, with Benito Famini, Sr. serving as the town's first mayor. Full and lasting independence followed a generation later: on 15 June 1968, Republic Act No. 5317 — sponsored by Congressman Jose D. Moreno — separated Calatrava from San Agustin and established it as an independent municipality.

Today Calatrava covers some 8,670 hectares, about 6.39% of the province's territory, and is made up of seven barangays: Balogo, Linao, Pagsangahan, Pangulo, Poblacion, San Roque and Talisay. It is bounded on the north by the Tablas Strait, on the east by San Agustin, and on the south and west by San Andres.
